claims.strategy: Geopolitical fade play — buy the oil dip on cancelled strikes, sell into Iran test
claims.crowd_belief: Peace rally is real. Oil at $90 is the new normal with strike risk removed.
claims.contradiction: Trump's strike-on, strike-off posture invites Iran to test resolve. Hormuz still disrupted. SPR release historically precedes escalation, not de-escalation. The crowd fading oil is repeating the 2022 playbook on the wrong side.

claims.strategy: Short rallies — war premium + chip compression unchanged by headline peace
claims.crowd_belief: Dow +700 confirms risk-on regime. Tech dip was a buying opportunity.
claims.contradiction: Dow +700 masks Oracle tumbling on data center costs, chip rout from valuation compression, and a war premium that hasn't resolved — the US is still bombing Iran (just not tonight). Rallies are exits.

claims.strategy: Long US energy complex — structural market share capture
claims.crowd_belief: Oil is cyclical. Hormuz reopens, prices normalize, US loses export advantage.
claims.contradiction: European and Asian buyers signed long-term US crude contracts. The US didn't win a quarter — it captured customers who will take years to unwind. $90 oil post-cancellation is the structural entry point.

claims.strategy: Short IPO pop — 91% loss margin at 96x revenue is untenable
claims.crowd_belief: SpaceX is the most anticipated IPO in history. Oversubscribed. Growth investors pile in.
claims.contradiction: SpaceX lost $4.28B on $4.69B revenue — a 91% loss margin. At $1.8T, that's 96x revenue. Barron's calls it 'hopes and dreams.' If SPCX debuts below $1.8T, it signals a regime shift in growth valuations — cascading through VC portfolios.

claims.strategy: Long defense — permanent baseline, not tactical cycle
claims.crowd_belief: Defense stocks already priced Iran escalation. Cancellation means risk premium fades.
claims.contradiction: Three-front combat (US-Iran, Israel-Iran, Israel-Hezbollah) is structural, not tactical. US NATO cuts + simultaneous Middle East engagement = defense industrial base must expand regardless of overnight headlines. LMT/GD budgets are structurally higher.
